title: Successive halving over restart starts
spec: Run the restart phase in rungs. Start with the 20 pooled relaxed starts and run a cheap SLSQP with MAX_ITER=40 on each. Keep the best 5 by sum of radii after repair. Then restart the best 5 from their current iterates with MAX_ITER=200 and keep the best overall. Stop each rung when the rung's time share runs out. Use the same time split as now, so the total CPU budget stays at 80% of time_limit.

title: Random swap of circles of different sizes
spec: Add a swap move to the basin-hopping phase. Pick two circles at random whose radii differ by more than 20 percent, exchange their centres, keep each radius attached to its index, and then run _solve_once on the swapped configuration with a small jitter. Radius-centre swaps of this kind move large circles into the slots left by small ones, which random Gaussian jitter rarely does. Keep the swap with probability 0.3 and use the normal jitter otherwise. Accept only if the best packing improves.

title: Interleaved restart and hop epochs
spec: Replace the two sequential phases with alternating epochs. Each epoch lasts a fixed slice of about 10 percent of the total budget. Odd epochs run one round of the pool restart as now, and even epochs run a block of basin-hopping steps from the current best. Both phases update the same best packing. Keep the 0.8 total time fraction and the 30 s limit, and keep the time checks based on process_time.

title: Riesz-energy continuation for starts
spec: Replace the penalty relaxation in _relax with a Riesz p-energy repulsion over the centres, sum over pairs of 1/d^p, plus a soft wall term. Minimise with L-BFGS-B while p increases through the sequence 6, 12, 24, 48, using the previous centres as the start for each p. Do this for each of the POOL random starts, then keep the KEEP lowest-energy configurations and pass them to SLSQP as before. This drives the starts toward well-spread configurations with a smooth schedule, and it uses no new packages.

title: Log-uniform multi-scale hop sizes
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, draw each hop's Gaussian sd from a log-uniform distribution over [0.005, 0.1] using rng, instead of the fixed HOP_SD=0.04. Small hops refine the basin and large hops escape it, and the mix needs no adaptation rule. Keep the acceptance rule of keeping the best packing unchanged.

title: Grow from an (n-1)-circle packing
spec: Before the restart phase, solve the (n-1)-circle problem with a short version of the existing pipeline, using about 15% of the restart budget. Take its best packing and insert the missing circle at the largest empty spot, found by evaluating the distance-to-nearest-centre-and-wall on a 100x100 grid. Set that circle's radius to the grid value. Then run _solve_once on the n-circle start, followed by the usual clip and _repair, and add the result to the candidate pool. Use only the seed for randomness.

title: Adaptive basin-hopping step size
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep HOP_SD as a variable instead of a constant. Track the acceptance rate of the last 20 hops, where a hop is accepted if it improves the best sum. If the rate is above 0.3, multiply HOP_SD by 1.2. If it is below 0.1, multiply by 0.8. Clamp HOP_SD to [0.005, 0.1]. Keep the 40% switch point and everything else the same.

title: Island model basin hopping
spec: Run three independent basin-hopping chains, each with its own current packing and its own rng stream spawned from the seed. Each chain runs in turn for a block of about 1/3 of the hopping time, measured with process_time. Each chain accepts a new local optimum only if its radius sum does not fall below its current value. After each round, every chain adopts the global best packing as its current state with probability 0.3 and keeps its own state otherwise. The global best is updated after every local solve. The restart phase and repair step stay as they are.

title: Rattler reinsertion into the largest hole
spec: After each local solve in basin hopping, find rattlers, meaning circles with no contact (gap below 1e-6 to any other circle or wall). For each rattler, sample 3000 uniform candidate points, pick the one whose distance to the nearest circle boundary is largest, and move the rattler there with radius set to that clearance. Re-run _solve_once from the modified packing and keep the result only if its repaired sum improves on the incumbent. Use rng for sampling.

title: Cluster crossover of two elite packings
spec: Keep the top 2 distinct packings found so far. Form a child by splitting the plane with a random line through (0.5,0.5), taking the circles of parent A on one side and of parent B on the other. If the count differs from n, remove the circles with the smallest radii or add random ones at the largest gap, then run _solve_once and _repair. Apply this with probability 0.2 in place of a Gaussian hop during basin hopping. This transfers good local structure between two basins that have already been optimised.

title: Partial-freeze SLSQP for local refinement
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, on each hop choose a random half of the circles and hold their centres fixed while SLSQP optimises the other half's centres and all radii. Implement this by building the SLSQP vector over only the free centres and radii, with the frozen centres inserted as constants inside cons. Run a second, unrestricted _solve_once from that result to finish. Each restricted solve has fewer variables and should converge faster, leaving more of the time budget for hops.

title: Per-start random SLSQP iteration budget
spec: In the random-restart phase, draw MAX_ITER per start from {80, 200, 500} using the seeded rng, so the pool mixes cheap and deep local solves. Pass the drawn value into _solve_once as a parameter instead of using the global. Keep the basin-hopping phase at MAX_ITER=200. The aim is to spend more time on promising deep solves while still sampling many basins.

title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP polish
spec: Replace the random-restart phase with a population search. Keep a population of 16 centre configurations (n x 2 arrays, drawn uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]) scored by _relax energy. For each generation, build a trial vector per member as a + F*(b - c) with three distinct random members and F=0.6, apply binomial crossover per circle with CR=0.9, clip to [0,1], run the cheap _relax on the trial, and keep it if its energy beats the member's. Every 10 generations, take the 3 lowest-energy members, run _solve_once, _repair them, and update best if the radius sum improves. Stop at the same time budget as before. All randomness comes from rng.

title: Quadrant decomposition starts
spec: Build a start by splitting the square into four quadrants. Assign n/4 circles to each quadrant (8 for n=32) and solve each quadrant as a separate small packing in the unit square using _solve_once with n/4 circles. Scale each quadrant solution into its own quadrant, then concatenate all centres and radii, and run _solve_once on the whole set of n circles to glue and polish. Include these decomposition starts with the existing random starts, and keep the best repaired result.

title: Wall-slide basin-hopping move
spec: Add a second hop type inside the basin-hopping loop, chosen with probability 0.25. Pick one random circle whose centre lies within 1.5 times its radius of a wall. Move it to a new uniform random position along that same wall (keep its perpendicular coordinate at the wall offset r_i), leave the other centres unchanged, and run _solve_once and _repair as usual. Keep the existing Gaussian hop for the other 75 percent of steps. Accept the result only if the radius sum improves, as the current code does.

title: Lightweight inner loop with penalty L-BFGS hops
spec: Use a cheap inner hop loop before the expensive SLSQP solve. For each basin-hopping step, perturb the incumbent with Gaussian noise of sd HOP_SD, then minimise a smooth penalty energy over centres and radii with L-BFGS-B, where the energy is the overlap squared plus wall violations squared minus a small weight times the radii sum. Keep the result only if its radii sum after _repair beats the incumbent, then call SLSQP only on every fifth accepted candidate. This increases the number of cheap hops by an order of magnitude while keeping SLSQP as the final polish.

title: Lubachevsky-style growth continuation
spec: Before SLSQP, run a jamming-style continuation for each start. Set a common radius R, starting at 0.6 of the relaxed value. Minimise the overlap energy with L-BFGS-B. Then increase R by a factor of 1.01 each step while the energy stays below 1e-10, and cut the step to 1.001 when it does not. Use the final centres and per-circle radii, capped by the wall distances, as the SLSQP starting point. Keep the restart and hop phases the same.

title: Population-based exploit-and-explore chains
spec: Run 4 basin-hopping chains with different hop sds (drawn from [0.01, 0.08] using the seeded rng) from 4 different restart packings. Every 10 hops, the chain with the worst best-sum copies the state (packing and hop sd) of the chain with the best best-sum, then perturbs its hop sd by a factor exp(N(0, 0.2)). The best packing over all chains is returned. Each hop is one _solve_once plus _repair as before. This population-based training moves the step size and the chain state together, combining the island and adaptive ideas in a way the earlier single-chain tests did not cover.

title: Target-radius energy relaxation for starts
spec: In the restart pool, call _relax with a per-start trial radius r0 drawn uniformly from [0.9, 1.3] times 0.5/sqrt(n) instead of the fixed r0. Starts from a too-small radius leave room to spread out, and starts from a too-large radius compress into different jammed basins. Keep the pool size and KEEP unchanged and draw all randomness from rng.

title: Randomised row-count strip starts
spec: Add a strip-based start generator. Choose a random number of rows between 4 and 7 and a random per-row circle count that sums to n (for example 5-6-5-6-5-5 style counts with random swaps). Place the centres in evenly spaced rows across [0.1, 0.9] in y with x positions spaced evenly within each row, then add uniform jitter of 0.03 and a random horizontal shear per row. Feed these into _relax and _solve_once as one of the start types in the restart pool, with about a third of the restart starts coming from this generator. This extends the hex-style seeding with variable row structure.

title: Bottom-left greedy fill starts
spec: Add a constructive start generator as an alternative to uniform random starts. Shuffle the circle indices and sort them into a random order of target radii, drawn from a uniform distribution on [0.06, 0.2]. Place them one at a time, each at the candidate point from a fixed grid of 400 points that maximises the largest radius feasible with the already placed circles, with ties broken toward the bottom-left corner. Store the resulting centres and their radii as the start for SLSQP. Use this generator for half of the restart starts, selected by the seed, and keep everything else unchanged.

title: Stratified jittered-cell starts
spec: For each restart start, divide the square into an n-cell grid. Use a random permutation from rng to place one centre per cell, jittered uniformly inside the cell with margin 0.1 from the cell edge. Feed these centres into the existing _relax pool in place of the uniform draws. Keep POOL and KEEP unchanged. This gives a stratified sample of centres with better coverage than purely uniform draws.

title: Max-min equal-radius pre-stage
spec: Before the random-restart SLSQP phase, run one extra SLSQP for each start in which all radii are tied to a single shared variable t and the objective is maximise t subject to the same non-overlap and wall constraints with r_i = t. This gives a feasible equal-radius packing that is far from the sum-optimal basin. Pass its centres, with radii initialised at t, into the normal SLSQP that maximises the sum. Use the same MAX_ITER and keep the existing repair step.

title: Penalty-weight homotopy in the SLSQP objective
spec: Add to the SLSQP objective a term -lambda times the sum of radius times the squared distance of each centre to (0.5, 0.5), with lambda annealed from 0.05 to 0 over three SLSQP calls. Each call starts from the previous solution. The final call is the plain objective, so the result is still a maximum of the sum of radii, but the first calls favour compact configurations that leave room for more radius. This is a continuation in the objective, not a new constraint.

title: Cyclic cosine hop-scale schedule
spec: Replace the fixed HOP_SD in basin hopping with a cosine-cycled scale. Over the hop phase, the sd follows s(t) = s_min + 0.5*(s_max - s_min)*(1 + cos(2*pi*k(t)/T_cycle)), with s_max = 0.08, s_min = 0.005 and T_cycle set to about 15 hops, so the scale restarts high after each cycle. When a hop improves the incumbent, reset the cycle phase to the start of a high-scale phase. This is a warm-restart schedule over step size, distinct from the adaptive or log-uniform variants.

title: Radius-scale rescaling of the basin-hopping step
spec: Instead of a fixed Gaussian sd HOP_SD for every centre, draw each hop's perturbation as sd proportional to the local slack, computed as the distance from each centre to its nearest neighbour minus the sum of the two radii, clipped to [0.2, 2] times HOP_SD. Circles with much room move more, and jammed ones move less. Keep the rest of the basin-hopping loop and the best-update rule unchanged.

title: Power-diagram starts weighted by target radii
spec: Add a start generator that draws n random sites in the square and n target radii from a Beta(2, 3) scaled to [0.05, 0.25]. Compute the power diagram with weights w_i = target_radius_i squared, approximated on a 200 by 200 grid by assigning each grid point to the site minimising |p - c_i|^2 - w_i. Set each centre to the centroid of its cell and each initial radius to the target value clipped by the distance to the nearest wall. Use this for about a quarter of restart starts before the standard SLSQP.

title: Log-barrier continuation before SLSQP
spec: Before the SLSQP call in _solve_once, run a short interior-point stage. Replace the hard pair and wall constraints with a log barrier -mu * sum(log(slack)) added to the objective -sum(r), using slack = distance minus radii sum for pairs and the wall distances for boundaries. Start mu at 1e-2 and divide by 10 for 4 to 5 stages, warm-starting each stage with L-BFGS-B from the previous solution and keeping r at least 1e-6. Then pass the barrier result to the existing SLSQP call as its start point. Use only the existing time budget and the same seeds, and do not change the repair step.

title: Gravity compaction hop in basin hopping
spec: Add a move to the basin-hopping loop with probability 0.25. Pick a random direction among the four walls (bottom, left, top, right) and a random angle in [0, pi/2] for diagonal directions. Sort the circles by their projection on the direction toward the wall. For each in order, slide its centre along the direction until it touches the wall or one of its radius-sum neighbours (use current radii), then leave the rest unchanged. Feed the compacted centres to _solve_once and _repair as usual. This simulates gravity-driven jamming, which can shift which circles are rattlers and open new contact networks.

title: Verlet molecular-dynamics quench of starts
spec: Replace the _relax energy minimisation for one third of the pool with a short molecular-dynamics run. Start from uniform random centres with zero velocity. Use soft repulsion between circles of fixed trial radius r0 = 0.5 over sqrt(n), a wall repulsion term, and velocity Verlet integration with timestep 0.01 for 300 steps. Apply a Berendsen thermostat that scales velocities by a factor that decays from 1.5 to 0 over the run (a slow cooling). Return the final positions, then pass them through the usual _relax and rank step. This mimics a thermal annealing of the packing and produces starts with a different spread of contacts than pure energy minimisation.

title: Covariance-guided evolution over centres, then SLSQP polish
spec: Replace the restart phase's uniform random draw with a small CMA-ES style search over the 2n centre coordinates. Keep a Gaussian with mean m (initially the best relaxed pool member) and per-coordinate sd sigma (initially 0.15). Each generation samples 12 candidates, scores each by running _relax from the candidate and taking its energy as fitness, then updates m and sigma from the best 4 using simple rank-weighted means and a multiplicative sigma step. After a fixed number of generations, polish the best candidate with _solve_once and _repair. This is a bolder global search that uses only numpy and scipy.

title: Log-sum-exp dispersion starts
spec: In the restart pool, replace the penalty relaxation for a third of the starts with a max-min dispersion solve: maximise a soft-min of pairwise centre distances plus boundary distances, implemented as minimising a log-sum-exp energy of -distance terms with L-BFGS-B. Increase the sharpness parameter beta in 3 steps (e.g. 5, 20, 80) with a warm start between steps. Initial radii for SLSQP are half the nearest-neighbour distance, clipped to the walls. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged and draw all randomness from the seeded rng.

title: Vogel sunflower spiral starts
spec: Add a start generator that places the n centres on a golden-angle (Vogel) spiral, p_k = 0.5 + s * sqrt(k + 0.5) * (cos(k * 2.39996...), sin(k * 2.39996...)) scaled to fit inside [0.1, 0.9]^2, then maps the points to the square by a radial rescale. Apply a random rotation angle, a random spiral scale s in [0.6, 1.0], and a jitter of sd 0.02 drawn from the seed. Use these as a fraction (about 25%) of the restart pool starts, relaxed with the existing _relax before SLSQP. Nothing else changes.

title: Wall-damped perturbation for hops
spec: Make the basin-hopping Gaussian kick depend on position. Compute for each centre its distance to the nearest wall, and multiply that circle's perturbation sd by a factor min(1, dist/0.2) with a floor of 0.2. Circles near the walls then move less and the interior moves more, so the kick breaks interior contacts while keeping the wall-touching frame. Keep HOP_SD as the base scale and the rest of the loop as it is. The change touches only the perturbation line.

title: Beta-distributed edge-biased starts
spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres in the restart pool with samples from a Beta(0.7, 0.7) distribution per coordinate, mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. This puts more starts near the walls and corners, where dense packings of 32 circles usually have their boundary circles. Keep the pool size, the _relax step and the KEEP selection unchanged. The change is one line in the sampling expression.

title: Lexicographic restart and polish schedule
spec: Replace the fixed 40 percent split with a loop of rounds of 10 percent of the budget: each round runs one restart pool and then one basin-hopping chunk of equal length from the current best, and the loop stops at the budget. Use the round index to select the pool size, with POOL = 10 for early rounds and 20 for late ones. This does not add moves, it only interleaves the two existing phases with a fixed, simple split.

title: Square grid with random holes as a start
spec: Add a start generator for the restart pool. Lay out a jittered square grid of about 6 by 6 sites spanning [0.1, 0.9] squared, then delete 4 random sites (chosen with rng) and add 4 uniform random points in the square to fill the holes, giving 32 centres in total. Add jitter of sd 0.02 to every centre. Use these as candidates in the pool with the same _relax filter as the others. Do not use the hex layout or the torus-wrap start, which are already in the backlog. The aim is starts that are near a lattice but have defects, which the SLSQP can then repair into different jammed configurations.

title: Largest-circle-anchored basin-hopping kick
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, choose the perturbation centre as the largest circle in the incumbent. Add Gaussian noise with the usual HOP_SD to all circles, but with probability 0.5 move only the 6 circles nearest to the largest one, leaving the rest fixed. Run the normal _solve_once and _repair on the result and keep the existing acceptance rule. This is a local kick around the most constrained region, not a global one.

title: Diagonal-mirror symmetric starts
spec: Generate a share of restart starts (about one third) that are symmetric under reflection across the diagonal y = x. Draw n/2 centres uniformly in the lower triangle and mirror them to (y, x). For odd n, put the extra centre on the diagonal at a random position. The mirrored starts are relaxed with the existing _relax and then optimised by SLSQP without any symmetry constraint, so the solver is free to break symmetry. Nothing else changes.

title: Cut-and-reflect hop
spec: Add a basin-hopping move that is chosen with probability 0.25. Draw a random line through the square. Reflect every circle centre on one side of the line across it, then clip centres to the square. Keep the radii unchanged, then run _solve_once and _repair as usual. The move breaks the symmetry of the incumbent and lets the local solver recombine halves of different arrangements. Keep the Gaussian hop as the other move.

title: Radius-cap continuation during restart SLSQP
spec: In _solve_once, add an upper bound on each radius that is annealed during the restart phase. Use a cap of 0.12 at the start of the round, then raise it geometrically to 1.0 by the final SLSQP iteration, implemented by running SLSQP in 3 stages with bounds r_i <= cap. Greedy early growth of a few large circles is what locks in poor basins, so the cap should let many circles settle before any one grows large. Keep the final stage uncapped so the repair and the returned packing are unchanged.
